newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's downgrades two Japan cement firms' ratings.
newsitem.headline: Moody's downgrades two Japan cement firms' ratings.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Wednesday it had downgraded Chichibu Onoda Cement's long-term debt rating to Ba2 from Ba1 and Nihon Cement's rating to Ba1 from Baa3.
Moody's also said it had maintained Sumitomo Osaka Cement's long-term debt rating at Ba2.
Moody's said the downgrading covered Chichibu's debt securities totalling 40 billion yen and its Japanese shelf registration with an authorised amount of 80 billion yen.

The downgrading reflected Moody's expectation that the cement firm's cash flow would remain depressed by an industry-wide overcapacity and a fall in domestic prices. The weakness of Chichibu's cash flow would inhibit the company's ability to reduce its heavy dependence on debt, it said.
Moody's said it also took into account the strength of Chichibu's business position as the largest cement producer in Japan and its geographically diversified earnings base.

Moody's said its downgrade of Nihon Cement reflected the rating agency's concern that sustained industry-wide overcapacity and lowering of domestic cement prices would, over time, reduce the company's cashflows, leading it to incur higher levels of debt to fund overseas expansion.
It said the downgrade of Nihon Cement covered debt securities totalling 88 billion yen and shelf registration in Japan authorising debt issue of 50 billion yen.
Moody's said its rating of Sumitomo Osaka Cement was based on an expected improvement in the company's operating performance based on cost cuts following the company's merger in 1994.
The rating on Sumitomo also reflects Moody's view that the Sumitomo group will give support to its cement company as necessary.
The Moody's rating of Sumitomo Osaka covers debt securities worth about 40 billion yen.
Moody's said the three ratings concluded a review initiated on May 28, 1996.
